chunk_map.heading: Phase 1: Read what the un-packaged run did
Make Claude show its work, make it dig
Phase 2: Match each failure to the check that catches it
Phase 3: Build the verifier for your worst failure
Phase 4: Write the reference and plan.md

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a reader loses the thread when a term/pronoun has no antecedent they can hold, including one that only points forward. Walked all 12 chunks. Chunk 0 (L15) 'the un-packaged run' and (L7) 'the worktree' are session artifacts from the immediately-preceding exercise in the SAME module's include order -- verified fork-the-worktree.md sits before diagnose-and-resend.md in learn-from-the-test.md (L50 vs L52) -- carve-out applies. Chunk 2 (L44) 'the repo read in Module 1' names a real cross-module beat by number and is maintainer-attested (raw L147, progression-with-variation note); verified orient-and-introspect.md is M1's own exercise (getting-going.md L44). Chunk 1's prompt (expanded, diagnose-and-resend-2) names the '"M4 starting point" commit' -- a session-artifact convention verified established in fork-the-worktree.md L39 / set-the-markers-send-it-off.md L27. Chunk 9 (L109) 'notice the prompt: it shrank' anticipates content shown two chunks later (ch10, {{prompt:ae101-m5-rerun-packaged}}) -- closest call in the file, but the file has already run the identical ask-then-prompt convention five times (ch1,3,4,5,7) by this point, so 'the prompt' resolves as the next instance of an established pattern, not an unnamed forward pointer of the 'before the three things get named' shape. Handles (verifier/reference/plan.md/packaging) all resolve within-file, first-defined then reused. No unresolved referent found. Harm absent.

Harm: a callback depending on which file/module sits where breaks under re-sequencing. Chunk 2 (L44) 'Module 1' -- named by number, claim unpacked in the same sentence ('assume about 10% of the account misrepresents the run'). Chunk 9 (L119) '[What packaging is](lectures/what-packaging-is.md)' -- navigational pointer naming the doc in its own link text, not located by position; file confirmed to exist. Chunk 10 (module-flag branch, L133) 'Module 6' -- named by number, confirmed a real module (spot-gaps-build-the-loop, site/layouts/curriculum.js L56), not positional phrasing ('the next module'). grep for positional phrases ('the opening lecture', 'earlier module', 'as you saw', etc.) across the body returned zero hits. Harm absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: 'the X you did/saw' pointing at a beat the module's current file set doesn't have strands the reader. Verified against site/layouts/curriculum.js (canonical 6-module AE101 registry, L49-56): M1=getting-going (orient-and-introspect.md confirmed its exercise, getting-going.md L44), M4=run-the-first-experiment, M5=learn-from-the-test (this file), M6=spot-gaps-build-the-loop -- all four beats this file names by number exist. 'M4 starting point' commit convention confirmed live in fork-the-worktree.md L39 and set-the-markers-send-it-off.md L27 ('Pin the starting point') and run-the-first-experiment.md L162. Chunk 10's flag:no-module branch (Module 6 absent) matches the real 'team-track' cut documented at site/layouts/curriculum.js L120-123, where M6 becomes a customer-authored workshop -- the runtime fork resolves against an actual registry variant, not an invented one. Harm absent.

Harm: a chunk that says nothing standalone projects as a blank beat. Closest candidate is the shortest chunk, ch8 'Approve' (L101-104, 9 words per scripts/check-slide-size.js --report): 'Say *lock it in.* The agent writes both files.' -- two complete sentences naming the action and its effect, not a wait-state or a context-dependent bullet fragment. No chunk in the 12-chunk walk consists only of a wait-state or a single context-dependent bullet. Harm absent.

Harm: a header that oversells or contradicts its own chunk misleads a reader who only reads headers. Spot-checked the terse ones: ch5 'Prove the verifier actually fires' -> content is exactly a smoke-test instruction + prompt firing the verifier. ch8 'Approve' -> content is the approval act ('Say lock it in'). ch10 'Send it off' -> content is the final re-send prompt plus post-send guidance. ch11 'Bring the worktree's work home' -> content is the CLAUDE.local.md/observations copy-back instruction. No header found that the chunk's own content contradicts. Harm absent.

Harm: cadence tics read as machine voice at slide density, one tic per slide is enough to trip. Checked all sub-items across all 12 chunks: no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction found; no anaphora/epistrophe triples found; no self-grading superlative found (grep for 'one of the most'/'most useful' etc. returned nothing); no abstraction-noun stack found; no verb-triplet-with-empty-leg found. The one number in the body, ch2 (L44) 'about 10%', carries no retraction clause here (unlike M1's 'could be more or less') -- the number+retraction sub-item requires a retraction to fire, and none is present, so it does not even reach the maintainer's M1-exemption question. Harm absent across every sub-item.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: repo/maintainer vocabulary on a projected slide is unparseable to the room. grep -niE for surface/firing/compendium/'forcing function'/beat(s)/mood/Connections across the body view returned exactly one hit: L19 'packaging you built against your own failure **beats** packaging you guessed at' -- the verb 'beats', not the noun 'beat' (pedagogical-unit dialect). No repo-internal term found on any slide. Harm absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: bold-as-decoration competes for attention and the reader can't tell what actually matters. The maintainer block's own 'Emphasis:' paragraph (raw L153) enumerates every bold span in the file, and it matches the body exactly: title-page labels + widget chrome (ch0, exempt from the per-slide budget as chrome); ch4's three verifier-shape handles LLM judge / Deterministic shell-hook / Ralph re-feed (all <=2 words) -- this is a pick-one menu ('Drop the shape name after the colon, one of: judge, shell-hook, Ralph re-feed'), so the reading-list/menu-slide carve-out applies and the per-slide budget is off, handle cap still met; ch6's two definitional handles Reference / plan.md (1 word each, introducing the two artifacts the rest of the exercise builds); ch7's two Phase-4 callout handles (stop-gate + timebox), maintainer-named as a pair. No undocumented bold found anywhere else in the body. TODO logged (non-blocking, this rule is non-blocking): ch7's first callout bolds the full sentence 'Cut the grill when the package is good enough to re-send.' (11 words, inside a `>` block) -- literally over the rule's stated <=5-word handle cap and arguably the kind of quote/callout the 'kickers/koans/quotes never bold' clause bans; the maintainer note treats it as a sanctioned handle alongside the 2-word 'Timebox check.', so no REVISE filed, but the gap between the rule's literal text and this attested usage is worth a compendium note.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran: node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/exercises/diagnose-and-resend.md --report -> 'slides: 10', composing 10 of the 11 body ## headers (drops ch11 'Bring the worktree's work home' under the default runtime-fork resolution, i.e. the flag:module:spot-gaps-build-the-loop branch, matching the canonical 6-module AE101 registry where M6 exists at site/layouts/curriculum.js L55-56). The excluded no-module branch is exactly the shape the real 'team-track' cut needs (M6 dropped, site/layouts/curriculum.js L120-123) -- both resolved variants are registry-backed, not invented. Rules 1-9 above were walked against every chunk regardless of which fork branch a given render resolves.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering — position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran: node scripts/check-slide-numbering.js --file curriculum/exercises/diagnose-and-resend.md -> 'OK — 1 files, Phase/Step numbering consistent.' Phase headers run 1,2,3,4,5 consecutively (L23,46,59,89,105); no hand-numbered header found; no in-body 'Phase K' cross-reference outside the headers themselves to go stale.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Page geometry dies at the cut; reading order survives.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran: node scripts/check-slide-deixis.js --file curriculum/exercises/diagnose-and-resend.md -> 'OK — 1 files, no page-geometry pointers across the slide cut.' Closest candidate: ch10 (L127) 'the re-send prompt below stands alone' -- the paste block ({{prompt:ae101-m5-rerun-packaged}}) sits at L131, inside the SAME chunk (Send it off, L125-137), which is the rule's own worked PASS example ('the prompt below' with the paste block on that slide is spatially true'). No cross-chunk geometry pointer found.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: In-deck links work now; whether they EARN their place is open.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran: node scripts/check-slide-deixis.js --file curriculum/exercises/diagnose-and-resend.md --links -> one in-body link, ch9 (L119) '[What packaging is](lectures/what-packaging-is.md)', named in its own link text, not located by page geometry; target file confirmed present at curriculum/lectures/what-packaging-is.md. Mechanism settled per the rule (not re-derived as broken); this is a review surface, not a gate.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide size — 210 words / 6 bullets, and the cap is machine-checked.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran: node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/exercises/diagnose-and-resend.md --report -> largest slide 'Phase 3: Build the verifier for your worst failure' at 191 words / 4 bullets, under the 210-word/6-bullet cap; 0 oversized across all 10 composed slides. No maintainer accept-note needed.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a declarative heading inside an exercise, or an imperative one on a law-slide, blurs the instructing/declaring split the whole corpus relies on. Walked all 11 body ## headers: five phase labels (Phase 1-5), five imperatives (Make Claude show its work make it dig / Prove the verifier actually fires / Approve / Send it off / Bring the worktree's work home), one catalogue-style subject-naming header ('The reference and plan.md', same shape as the rule's own exempt examples 'Ralph' / 'The numbers'). No declarative-claim header found -- consistent with an exercise file that names no law/consolidation beat of its own. Harm absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a bullet that re-announces doctrine, narrates the curriculum's own design, or closes with a header-restating koan reads as rigour while adding nothing. Closest candidate: ch2 (L44) 'The same moment may carry more than one lens' echoes the prompt's own instruction to Claude in ch1 ('The same moment may support more than one lens; explain what each lens reveals') -- but it serves a distinct student-facing function (sets the student's expectation for reviewing Claude's output) rather than re-announcing a law already done working, so it is not class (a). Ch0's '**The point:**' line (L19) is opening thesis framing, not a closing koan restating a header, so not class (c). No self-referential design commentary (class b) found -- the file never narrates its own pedagogy to the student. No violation found.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a guess-before-reveal instruction whose answer is narrated above it spoils the beat on a text read. Read all 12 chunks: the file's shape is diagnose -> match -> build -> prove -> assemble -> resend; no guess/predict-then-reveal construction exists anywhere in body. Rule doesn't apply.
